notes:
ScreenTale 1.13.0 gives each Camera clip its own layout, moves the camera bubble out of the cursor's way, and makes recording and exporting lighter and faster.

- Camera clips now own their layout. Select a Camera clip on the Timeline to choose Picture in Picture, Side by Side or Full Screen and style its bubble for that clip. To change the layout part-way, split the clip. The Camera Changes row is gone; older projects open with their Camera clips split so they look exactly as before.
- New Avoid cursor: the Picture in Picture bubble slides aside while the recorded cursor is near it, then returns, in both the preview and exports. It is on by default; choose the direction in Settings > Camera, or override it for one project in the Camera Inspector.
- Annotations now follow the pointer while you drag them in the preview.
- Every Inspector colour uses one colour picker with suggested swatches, the macOS colour panel, a hex field and an Opacity slider.
- Annotation layers are shown in a compact Layers list where you can show, hide, lock, rename, reorder and delete them.
- ScreenTale no longer saves projects automatically. An Edited badge shows unsaved changes, Save (⌘S) saves them, and closing, switching projects or quitting asks whether to save.
- Dragging and resizing in the Fixed Zoom navigator works again.
- New Recording size setting (Compact, Balanced or Maximum) in Settings > Recording. New installations start at Balanced and 30 fps for smaller recordings. Camera footage is recorded at 1080p.
- Recordings look sharper at the same file size, and recorded audio is stored as Apple Lossless, which takes far less space with no loss in quality.
- You can hide the floating camera preview while recording; the camera keeps recording.
- Turning the microphone on or off, or switching cameras, no longer reloads the camera preview.
- Video exports are faster, and GIF exports finish several times faster.
- GIF export works again, and an intermittent "media backend failed" export error is fixed.
